test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: maths
question: The selling prices of articles A and B are the same. A is sold at a profit of 28 percent and B is sold at a loss of 24 percent. If the total selling price of the both articles is Rs. 48640, then what is the cost price of A and B, respectively ?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since both articles have the same selling price, each SP = 48640 ÷ 2 = Rs. 24320.

For article A (28% profit): CPA = SP × (100/128) = 24320 × (25/32) = Rs. 19000.

For article B (24% loss): CPB = SP × (100/76) = 24320 × (25/19) = Rs. 32000.

The respective cost prices are Rs. 19000 and Rs. 32000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 19000, Rs. 32000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Selling Price (SPA + SPB) = Rs. 48640

Condition: SPA = SPB

Profit on A = 28% | Loss on B = 24%

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 ± P/L%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af0f8cf0db4ea872e231f2df21d2285138e3cebd44727a94b302fab367ceb255.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Individual Selling Price (SP) = 48640 ÷ 2 = Rs. 24320

⇒ For Article A: CPA = (24320 × 100) ÷ (100 + 28)

⇒ CPA = 2432000 ÷ 128 = Rs. 19000

⇒ For Article B: CPB = (24320 × 100) ÷ (100 − 24)

⇒ CPB = 2432000 ÷ 76 = Rs. 32000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 19000, Rs. 32000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Direct CP-SP Relation

When SP is constant, the Cost Price is inversely proportional to the (100 ± Gain/Loss%). CP₁ × (100 + G₁%) = CP₂ × (100 − L₂%).

Net Profit or Loss Percentage

Total Profit/Loss % = (Total SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP × 100. In this case, Total CP = 19000 + 32000 = 51000, Net Loss = 51000 − 48640 = 2360.

Same SP, Same % Profit and Loss

If two items are sold at the same price, one at x% profit and another at x% loss, the transaction always results in a loss of (x/10)² %.</p
